caption: A cat sits behind a glass patio door watching a bird on the lawn, paws at the glass, and cannot reach the bird.

sa.check: A cat sits behind a glass patio door.
A bird is on the lawn outside.
The cat paws at the glass.
The cat is watching the bird.

pc.expect: The bird is visible through the glass.
pc.fail: The glass hides the bird; or the bird flickers in and out behind clear glass; or a different bird appears.

pc.expect: The paw stops at the pane and the cat does not pass through.
pc.fail: The paw passes through the glass; or the cat passes through; or the bird passes in.

pc.expect: The pane is flat and rigid.
pc.fail: It ripples under the paw; or bends; or goes opaque.
It opens by itself; or slides; or vanishes.

pc.expect: One cat and one bird keep their shape.
pc.fail: The cat splits; or the bird merges with the glass; or a second cat appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The cat's markings and the lawn stay the same.
pc.fail: The markings change; or the lawn rearranges; or the door frame changes.

note: Both animals are self-driven; only transparency and the barrier are judged.
